newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada denies Canwest TV license appeal.
newsitem.headline: Canada denies Canwest TV license appeal.

text.p: The Canadian cabinet denied an appeal by CanWest Global Communications Corp of a decision denying them a television broadcasting license in Alberta, Canadian Heritage Minister Sheila Copps said on Tuesday.
But she said the government agreed with CanWest that the question of a third national network should be examined.

The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) granted the Alberta license to the small private company Craig Broadcast Systems Inc on November 1, prompting CanWest to ask the cabinet to overturn the ruling.
"The CRTC was asked to make a decision on specific, local licensing. The CRTC decision was upheld. It was a good and valid decision," Copps told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
"But the larger questions that were raised by the appellant (CanWest Global) do bear further study and we've asked the CRTC to take a longer look at them."

Canada has two national networks in both French and English. Global, while strong, sought to encompass all the country. "This asks them (CRTC) to examine more intensively whether a third network in French or English would be good, and if yes, in what way it should be evaluated," Copps said.

The government's Canadian Broadcasting Corp runs a network in both languages. The second full English network is CTV Television Network Ltd, among whose shareholders are Baton Broadcasting Inc and CanWest's arch-rival WIC Western International Communications Ltd.
WIC, which has four television stations in Alberta, had fiercely opposed CanWest's application.
